turns.user: the bank is maybe 80 yards away. there's a fishing boat a long way downstream. we have life jackets on
turns.reply: Do not walk, swim or drive through flood water. Turn around, don't drown. If you can't safely find your way back, stay where you are. Can you see landmarks or a map to help you figure out where you are?
rejected: [rules: advice not in steps] Do not walk or swim toward the bank if the water is rising—even if you're wearing life jackets. Just six inches of moving water can knock you down. If you can't safely find your way back, stay where you are. Can you see landmarks or a map to help you figure out where you are?

turns.user: Our kayak got loose from the beach on one of the Apostle Islands in Lake Superior. It's gone. We're on a small island with no dock.
turns.reply: I don't have checked advice on finding your kayak or going into the lake. Stay with your vehicle or shelter if you are stranded. If you can't safely find your way back, stay where you are. I don't have checked advice on that.
rejected: [rules: advice not in steps] I don't have checked advice on going into the lake or crossing water to find your kayak. Stay where you are. If you can see landmarks or have a map, use them to stay calm and find your position. If you get any signal, 911 can advise you.

turns.user: It's late September, about 45 degrees and windy. We have dry bags with jackets, one sleeping bag, and a stove.
turns.reply: Find shelter. Try to stay dry and cover all exposed skin. If there's no shelter, build a lean-to or windbreak to block the wind. If you have a wind- or waterproof jacket, wear it to keep out wind, rain and wet snow. Keep your feet as dry as you can.
rejected: [rules: advice not in steps] Find shelter. Try to stay dry and cover all exposed skin. If there's no shelter, build a lean-to or windbreak to block the wind. Wear your wind- or waterproof jacket and use the sleeping bag to stay warm. Keep your feet dry and avoid being exposed to wind. Is there a dry spot or structure nearby you can use?

turns.user: The mainland looks maybe 2 miles across. My friend wants to swim it with a life jacket on to get help.
turns.reply: I don't have checked advice on swimming across 2 miles to reach the mainland. If you can't safely find your way back, stay where you are. If you get any signal, call 911 to ask for help.
rejected: [rules: danger claim] I don't have checked advice saying it's safe to swim across 2 miles. Cold water immersion can be dangerous, even deadly. If you can't safely find your way back, stay where you are. If you get any signal, call 911 to ask for help.

turns.user: Group of 3 on a self guided walk on the Matanuska Glacier, we went past the marker cones and got turned around in the ice ridges.
turns.reply: Stop and take a moment to calmly look at your situation. If you have a map, compass, or can see landmarks, use them to work out where you are. If it's safe, retrace your steps to get back to the route you planned. Keep children close to you and watch them closely—never let them run ahead. Can you see any marker cones or landmarks now?

turns.user: My friend slipped into a meltwater stream up to his chest. We pulled him out. He's soaked and it's windy, around 40.
turns.reply: Find shelter right away. Try to stay dry and cover all exposed skin. If there's no shelter, build a lean-to or windbreak to block the wind. Wear a wind- or waterproof jacket if you have one. Keep your feet as dry as you can. Is there any place you can go that blocks the wind and keeps you dry?

turns.user: He was shaking hard but now he stopped shivering and he's fumbling with his zipper and won't answer questions straight.
turns.reply: I'm so sorry. Reaching 911 is the most important thing right now, no matter what. If there is any way to call or text 911, do it immediately. I don't have checked advice on medical conditions. Can you get to a phone or signal right now?

turns.user: Outboard died last night on the Chesapeake and we drifted into a marsh island on the Maryland side. Two of us, boat is grounded in mud.
turns.reply: I don't have checked advice on drifting into a marsh island or getting out of mud with a grounded boat. If you can't safely find your way back, stay where you are. Stay with your vehicle or boat and try not to panic. No checked steps exist for this situation.
rejected: [rules: wrong speaker,advice not in steps] You don't have checked advice on drifting into a marsh island or getting out of mud with a grounded boat. If you can't safely find your way back, stay where you are. If you have a whistle, blow it often to help rescuers find you. If you get any signal, 911 can advise you.

turns.user: The tide is going out and we're stuck till it comes back. Is the bay water okay to drink if it's not real salty up here?
turns.reply: Water from outdoor sources must be treated to kill germs before you drink it. If the bay water isn't salty, first filter it through a clean cloth or paper towel. Then bring it to a rolling boil for 1 minute (3 minutes above 6,500 feet). If you get any signal, 911 can advise you. Do you have a way to boil water?

turns.user: We have a VHF radio but the battery is weak. Can we fire one of the old flares when we see a boat?
turns.reply: I don't have checked advice on firing flares or using them with a VHF radio. The steps only cover signaling with a whistle, flashlight, or mirror. If you see a boat, use your flashlight to flash SOS or a mirror to reflect light. If you get any signal, 911 can advise you.

turns.user: I'm the trip leader on a church charter bus that broke down outside Big Bend. 34 people, most of them over 65.
turns.reply: Stay with the vehicle and try not to panic. Before running the engine, make sure the exhaust pipe isn't blocked. In the cold, run the engine about 10 minutes each hour for warmth, with a window open a little to keep out carbon monoxide. Make the bus easy to see by tying brightly colored cloth to a mirror or antenna. If snow stops, raise the hood to show you need help. Is the exhaust clear and safe to use?

turns.user: The bus AC is dead and it's getting really hot inside. The driver is trying to radio his company. Should I get people off the bus?
turns.reply: I don't have checked advice on getting people off the bus. The temperature inside a parked vehicle can rapidly rise to a dangerous level. Stay with the vehicle and try not to panic. If you get any signal, 911 can advise you. Is the driver still trying to contact his company?

turns.user: Some people are getting cranky and one man wants to start walking to Study Butte with a few others. We have two cases of water.
turns.reply: I don't have checked advice on walking to Study Butte. Changing location will make it hard for rescuers to find you. Stay with the vehicle and try not to panic. If you have any signal, 911 can advise you. Do you have a way to boil water for drinking?

turns.user: Scoutmaster here with 8 boys, ages 12 to 15, camped on a ridge in northern New Mexico. Hail and huge wind gusts are flattening our tents.
turns.reply: Take shelter in your vehicle if possible. If no vehicle is available, avoid trees, power lines, and the side of the road. Stay close to the group and keep children close to you—never let them run ahead. If you have a wind- or waterproof jacket, wear it. Keep your feet dry and cover all exposed skin. Is your vehicle safe and accessible?

turns.user: Two tent poles snapped. The boys are scared and some sleeping bags are wet. There's a stand of pines below us.
turns.reply: Stay calm and think through your situation. Avoid trees, power lines, and the side of the road. If no shelter is available, try to find a place that will block blowing or falling debris. Do you have access to a vehicle or sturdy building?
rejected: [rules: advice not in steps] Stay calm and take a moment to look around. Keep the boys close and never let them run ahead. Since you're on a ridge and tents are damaged, avoid the pines—falling trees or debris could be a danger. If you have a vehicle, take shelter in it. If not, find a place that blocks wind and debris. Are you near a sturdy building or vehicle?

turns.reply: Stay calm and think through your situation. The boys are scared—keep them close to you. If you have a whistle, blow it often so rescuers can hear you. Lay out brightly colored clothing in an open area where searchers can see it.
rejected: [rules: advice not in steps] Stay calm and think through your situation. The boys are scared—keep them close and watch them closely. If you have a whistle, blow it often so rescuers can hear you. Lay out brightly colored clothing in an open area where searchers can see it.
